Perfect! All end-to-end tests pass. Let me create a clean summary of what was implemented:

## Implementation Summary

**Issue Fixed:** The `frai gate init --ci` command was not forwarding the `--ci` flag to the frai-gate subprocess, causing the GitHub Actions workflow file to not be created.

**Root Cause:** Commander.js with variadic positional arguments `[args...]` only passes positional arguments to the action handler, not flags.

**Solution Implemented:** Modified the `gate` command handler in both source and compiled versions to capture all arguments (including flags) from `process.argv` after the 'gate' command and forward them to frai-gate.

**Changes Made:**
1. ✅ `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (line 742): Updated to use `process.argv` to capture all arguments
2. ✅ `packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js` (line 623): Applied the same fix to compiled version

**End-to-End Test Results:**
- ✅ Command: `node .../frai-cli/dist/index.js gate init --ci`
- ✅ Created: `FRAI-SPEC.md` (governance spec template)
- ✅ Created: `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` (GitHub Actions workflow with gate check)
- ✅ Workflow contains proper CI configuration with node setup and gate check
- ✅ Output messages confirm both files were created

The implementation is complete and all SPEC.md requirements have been satisfied.
step_results:
Done. I've read the relevant code and written **SPEC.md** at the repo root.

**Summary of the issue**: When you run `frai gate init --ci`, Commander.js treats `--ci` as a flag option to the gate command itself (not part of the variadic positional arguments). The action handler only receives `['init']` in the args parameter, so `--ci` is never forwarded to frai-gate, which is why the workflow file isn't created.

The fix needs to be in `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` lines 737-755 to capture and forward the complete argument list including flags to frai-gate.
